battles.title: The Italian advance into Egypt

pre.objective: The Italian Tenth Army was ordered into Egypt; the British screen was to delay and warn without sacrificing the mobile force needed to defend Matruh.
pre.forces: The advance used Libyan divisions, Maletti's mobile group and Italian reserves. The British screen included the 7th Armoured Support Group and 11th Hussars.
pre.deployment: The British Support Group observed the Sollum–Fort Maddalena frontier. Italian forces assembled west of Sollum; the 4th Blackshirt and 64th Catanzaro divisions remained near Tobruk as reserves.

timeline.event: Italian troops took Musaid and advanced through Sollum after an artillery opening.
The Italian advance reached Sidi Barrani and then halted.

post.outcome: Italy held a forward position at Sidi Barrani but did not continue to Matruh. British mobile forces withdrew in good order toward their planned defence.
post.why: Road and water works, limited motor transport and a British delaying screen constrained the advance.

battles.limits: The full 13 September unit roster, strength returns and exact 10 km deployment are not validated.

battles.title: Nibeiwa, Tummar and Sidi Barrani

pre.objective: Western Desert Force planned a surprise attack through the gap between Italian camps, destroying Nibeiwa and Tummar before turning on Sidi Barrani.
pre.forces: 4th Indian Division, 7th Armoured Division and 7th Royal Tank Regiment faced the Maletti Group, two Libyan divisions and other Italian camp defenders. 16th British Brigade remained after 4th Indian Division's departure.
pre.deployment: The Italian camps lay separately at Nibeiwa, Tummar, Maktila, Rabia and Sofafi. British armour and infantry assembled south of the camps for the concealed approach.

timeline.event: 11th Indian Brigade and 7th RTR overran Nibeiwa; the tanks then attacked Tummar West that afternoon.
Tummar East was occupied and Sidi Barrani town fell late in the day.
Isolated Italian positions continued surrendering after the town's fall.

post.outcome: The Italian camp system around Sidi Barrani was broken and the Commonwealth advance could continue toward Bardia.
post.why: Surprise, separated camps and the concentrated infantry-tank assault let a smaller force defeat the local positions in sequence.

battles.limits: The game cannot reproduce 7th RTR's two same-day assaults or distinguish working tanks from temporarily unserviceable ones. 4th Indian Division's historical 14 December departure is beyond this battle record but remains in the period timeline and research note.

battles.title: The assault on Bardia

pre.objective: 6th Australian Division was ordered to breach Bardia's central and southern defences, capture the town and overcome the remaining perimeter; the Italian garrison sought to hold the fortress and port.
pre.forces: 16th and 17th Australian Brigades, 7th RTR, engineers and artillery made the principal assault; 19th Australian Brigade covered and followed. Italian formations included parts of the Blackshirt, Marmarica, Cirene and Catanzaro divisions with fortress troops.
pre.deployment: The Italians occupied an extensive perimeter, posts, artillery and the town. The first Australian phase attacked the western and southern sector rather than the town alone.

timeline.event: The Australian attack breached the perimeter in two planned phases.
Bardia town was captured late in the day while resistance persisted farther south.
The southern perimeter's remaining resistance ended.

post.outcome: The Commonwealth captured Bardia and its garrison; the pursuit toward Tobruk proceeded.
post.why: A prepared infantry, engineer, artillery and tank assault broke the perimeter, then cleared positions that remained after the town fell.

battles.limits: The source's roughly 45,000 defenders and 23 serviceable 7th RTR tanks are aggregate and availability figures, not individual game counter strengths. The trial's 10 km hexes cannot represent perimeter posts, mines or breaches.

battles.title: The capture of Tobruk

pre.objective: The Commonwealth aimed to capture Tobruk's fortified port and continue west; the Italian XXII Corps and garrison sought to hold its perimeter and harbour.
pre.forces: 6th Australian Division's brigades, supported by 7th RTR, artillery and air forces, attacked an Italian defence including 61st Sirte Division, fortress troops and guns. The 7th Armoured Division screened the western approaches.
pre.deployment: The Australian attack faced an outer defended perimeter south of the port. Armoured forces moved by the inland Capuzzo–El Adem route while the Australians approached along the coast-road axis.

timeline.event: The detailed Australian official history describes the main perimeter assault on this day.
Australian forces entered Tobruk and the Italian command surrendered in the detailed official account.

post.outcome: Tobruk fell and became the Commonwealth's forward port for the Cyrenaican pursuit.
post.why: A breach of the perimeter and the collapse of the Italian inner defence opened the town and harbour; the armoured screen limited retreat westward.

disputed.point: Date of the assault and fall

accounts.claim: Assault on 21 January; town taken on 22 January
Assault on 22 January; town taken on 23 January

battles.limits: The detailed Australian official history places the assault and fall on 21–22 January; the AWM overview describes 22–23 January. The discrepancy is preserved for source review. Italian garrison totals and game-counter strengths are not interchangeable.

battles.title: The pursuit through Mechili and Derna

pre.objective: Commonwealth forces pursued the Italian withdrawal west from Tobruk, seeking the roads through Mechili and Derna; Axis rearguards attempted to delay them.
pre.forces: 7th Armoured Division advanced on the inland route and 6th Australian Division moved on the northern routes. Italian rearguards included 60th Sabratha and Babini armour in contemporary reports.
pre.deployment: The armoured route ran toward Mechili; Australian formations moved through the Jebel Akhdar approaches to Derna. Exact dated strengths and locations of the western Italian groups remain open.

timeline.event: The westward pursuit continued after Tobruk, with armoured movement toward Mechili and an Australian advance on the northern roads.
Commonwealth troops entered Derna after rearguard fighting.

post.outcome: Derna passed to the Commonwealth and the Italian withdrawal continued toward Benghazi and Beda Fomm.
post.why: The northern infantry pursuit and inland armoured movement threatened the remaining Italian routes, though transport constrained how quickly Australian brigades could move.

battles.limits: The game's 23 January entry date for western Axis counters is a modelling device, not evidence of their arrival in Libya. Their identities and strengths still need dated records.

battles.title: The road block at Beda Fomm

pre.objective: The Commonwealth aimed to intercept the Italian withdrawal from Benghazi before it escaped south; Italian forces sought to keep the coast road open.
pre.forces: 7th Armoured Division made the inland interception while 6th Australian Division pursued through the Jebel Akhdar. The Italian retreat comprised the remaining Cyrenaican field forces, whose local composition and serviceability varied.
pre.deployment: Aircraft observed Italian columns withdrawing west from Benghazi. British armour moved from Mechili toward the coast-road crossing near Beda Fomm.

timeline.event: Air reconnaissance found the Italian withdrawal; O'Connor accelerated the armoured interception.
The road block held and Italian surrender followed by the morning.

post.outcome: The Italian withdrawal was cut at Beda Fomm and the remaining Cyrenaican field force surrendered.
post.why: The inland armoured move reached the coast road ahead of the retreat while Australian pursuit kept pressure from the north.

battles.limits: The engine does not model army-scale surrender when one road hex is reached. Australian transport shortages allowed only part of the infantry to advance quickly at once.

battles.title: The April reversal across Cyrenaica

pre.objective: Axis forces pressed east from Mersa Brega; Commonwealth commanders were ordered to delay while preserving their reduced field force and Tobruk.
pre.forces: 2nd Armoured Division and 9th Australian Division faced German and Italian mobile formations. The British armoured force was weak and short of serviceable vehicles; the Australians lacked equipment and transport.
pre.deployment: The British Support Group held Mersa Brega through 31 March, then withdrew. The following defence and withdrawal routes ran through Benghazi, Mechili and toward Tobruk.

timeline.event: German forces occupied Mersa Brega after the British withdrawal.
German reconnaissance reached Benghazi as the Commonwealth retreat continued.
Axis forces reached the Tobruk area while the port's defence held.

post.outcome: The Commonwealth lost most of Cyrenaica but retained Tobruk, which became a besieged port.
post.why: A thin, mechanically weak defence withdrew under mobile pressure; holding Tobruk preserved a coastal obstacle to Axis supply and advance.

battles.limits: The game carries whatever front the player has made. Its April entry dates, strengths and 10 km positions are partly estimated, and a map approach to Tobruk is not a siege model.

battles.title: The opening battles of the Tobruk siege

pre.objective: The 9th Australian garrison was to deny Tobruk's port to the Axis and delay its advance; Axis commanders sought to seize the fortress.
pre.forces: 9th Australian Division, reinforced by 18th Australian Brigade and other Commonwealth troops, defended the perimeter against German and Italian forces including 5th Light, 15th Panzer, Ariete and Brescia elements.
pre.deployment: The defenders held Tobruk's perimeter posts, minefields and harbour while supply arrived by sea. Axis attacks focused on selected perimeter sectors rather than the whole 10 km map hex.

timeline.event: The Easter attack was repelled after fighting around the perimeter.
A renewed Axis attack began around Ras el Medauar and the salient.
The battle for the salient had not yielded Tobruk's port to the Axis.

post.outcome: The Axis failed to take Tobruk in the opening siege battles; the garrison continued to hold and be supplied by sea.
post.why: Prepared posts, minefields, artillery and naval supply let the garrison withstand attacks against limited sectors.

battles.limits: The trial has no local perimeter-post, mine-breach or naval-resupply battle model. Its opening roster is a carried campaign state, not a validated 12 April deployment.

battles.title: Operation Brevity

pre.objective: Wavell ordered a frontier attack to clear Sollum and Capuzzo, inflict losses and exploit toward Tobruk only if supply and the safety of the force allowed.
pre.forces: 7th Armoured Brigade Group, 22nd Guards Brigade Group with 4th RTR infantry tanks, and a coast group built around 2nd Rifle Brigade and artillery made the Commonwealth attack. Axis troops defended the frontier and could counterattack.
pre.deployment: The British plan used a desert flank, a central attack and a coastal group against Halfaya, Sollum and Capuzzo.

timeline.event: The Commonwealth frontier attack began.
Axis counterattack and British withdrawal followed the initial gains.

post.outcome: The short attack did not open a lasting route to Tobruk.
post.why: The operation was a bounded probe with limited forces and supply, and Axis reaction prevented exploitation.

battles.limits: The 29 cruiser and 24 infantry tanks are source figures for particular groups; the game's manpower, entry hexes and 5 May preparation arrivals are estimates.

battles.title: The Halfaya counterstroke

pre.objective: Axis forces sought to retake Halfaya Pass after the British frontier probe; the Commonwealth aimed to keep its forward foothold.
pre.forces: German and Italian frontier troops faced the British groups left around Halfaya and Sollum after Brevity. A complete dated local roster still needs verification.
pre.deployment: Halfaya was the escarpment pass controlling the coastal route; its approaches could be defended from above and below the escarpment.

timeline.event: German troops attacked the Halfaya position.
Axis troops recovered Halfaya Pass.

post.outcome: Halfaya returned to Axis control before Battleaxe.
post.why: The counterattack displaced the limited British frontier force and restored the Axis defensive position at the pass.

battles.limits: The linked chapter spans 18–27 May; only 26–27 May is the dated historical counterstroke. Local force strengths and map-scale fortifications remain open.

battles.title: Operation Battleaxe

pre.objective: Wavell planned first to defeat the Axis frontier force and secure the Bardia–Sollum–Capuzzo area, then attack forces near Tobruk and exploit west if the first phase succeeded.
pre.forces: 4th Indian Division, 7th Armoured Division, 7th RTR and other Commonwealth groups faced 15th Panzer, 5th Light, Italian mobile troops and prepared frontier positions. The official history gives roughly 90 cruiser and 100 infantry tanks at the start, not counter-level readiness.
pre.deployment: The British assault had a coastal Halfaya attack, a Capuzzo centre and an armoured desert flank toward Hafid Ridge. Axis anti-tank positions, mines and mobile reserves defended the approaches.

timeline.event: The attack failed at Halfaya, gained ground at Capuzzo and was checked at Hafid Ridge.
Axis mobile counterattacks struck while Commonwealth armour and infantry tried to consolidate.
The Commonwealth offensive was called off without relieving Tobruk.

post.outcome: Battleaxe failed to open the route to Tobruk; the frontier and siege remained contested.
post.why: Concealed anti-tank guns, mines, breakdowns and Axis mobile reaction disrupted the three-pronged plan, while gains at Capuzzo could not be exploited.

battles.limits: The game lacks detailed tank serviceability, concealed gun positions, Hafid Ridge terrain and a second-phase Tobruk attack. Its 1 June reinforcement date and exact strengths are model estimates.

battles.title: Operation Crusader

pre.objective: Eighth Army sought to destroy Axis armour, relieve Tobruk and retake Cyrenaica; Axis forces sought to keep the siege and their frontier position.
pre.forces: XXX and XIII Corps, New Zealand and South African divisions and army tank brigades faced 15th and 21st Panzer, Ariete, Trieste and other Axis formations. The linked campaign's exact counter strengths and entry dates are not historical returns.
pre.deployment: The Eighth Army assembled east of the frontier and advanced toward Sidi Rezegh and Tobruk; Axis mobile formations were dispersed around the siege and frontier and later concentrated in reaction.

timeline.event: Eighth Army opened Crusader with an advance into Cyrenaica.
New Zealand troops linked toward the Tobruk garrison after taking Sidi Rezegh and Belhamed.
The New Zealand Division withdrew from Libya after heavy fighting.
The Tobruk siege was lifted in the historical campaign.
Commonwealth forces retook Benghazi during the westward pursuit.

post.outcome: Tobruk was relieved and Axis forces withdrew across Cyrenaica.
post.why: Attritional mobile fighting, pressure from the Tobruk garrison and Eighth Army's continued advance broke the siege and forced an Axis withdrawal.

battles.limits: The independent Crusader start and linked campaign start are different. The linked trial's relief corridor, reinforcement readiness and losses remain game abstractions.

battles.title: The fighting at Sidi Rezegh and Belhamed

pre.objective: The Commonwealth advance sought the Sidi Rezegh airfield and a connection to Tobruk; Axis troops sought to deny the route and defeat the attacking armour.
pre.forces: 7th Armoured Brigade and New Zealand formations fought around the airfield and Point 175; German panzer divisions, Afrika Division infantry, Italian armour around Bir el Gubi and Tobruk garrison troops reacted. Exact 18 November regimental locations remain under review.
pre.deployment: On 18 November the airfield was not held by the full German infantry formation later fighting nearby. Ariete was around Bir el Gubi; German troops around the Tobruk siege ring moved toward the airfield after the British advance.

timeline.event: 7th Armoured Brigade seized the Sidi Rezegh airfield against light resistance.
New Zealand troops fought a costly action at Point 175.
New Zealand forces took Sidi Rezegh and Belhamed and linked toward Tobruk.
Axis counterattacks began against the New Zealand-held positions and continued after this short scenario's historical window.

post.outcome: A temporary link toward Tobruk was made by 26 November; Axis counterattacks then contested the relief positions. The wider siege ended in December.
post.why: The airfield's light initial defence allowed early seizure, but nearby Axis mobile forces and siege troops could counter-concentrate around the narrow relief route.

battles.limits: The five-turn game deadline, vehicle corridor and 10 km places are playable abstractions. Historical positions changed by day; later German occupancy cannot be projected back onto the 18 November opening.

battles.title: The January Axis counteroffensive

pre.objective: Axis command launched a limited counterattack to regain Cyrenaican ground; Eighth Army sought to protect its force and hold Tobruk and the Egyptian approaches.
pre.forces: Afrika Korps and 90th Light, with Italian mobile forces, faced British armoured and infantry formations; the trial lacks reliable unit-level serviceable strength returns for this operation.
pre.deployment: After Crusader, Axis forces lay around the Marada–Mersa Brega line while Commonwealth formations occupied the ground farther east.

timeline.event: The Axis counterattack began.
Benghazi was retaken in Toppe's account.
The advance halted short of Tobruk.

post.outcome: The Axis recovered Agedabia, Benghazi and Derna but stopped before attacking Tobruk.
post.why: Fuel shortage and the condition of the troops limited further pursuit.

battles.limits: The New Zealand timeline dates Benghazi's recapture to 29 January, one day earlier than Toppe's 30 January. The game does not force either date or reconstruct repair and fuel flows.

battles.title: Gazala and the fall of Tobruk

pre.objective: Rommel sought to defeat Eighth Army armour, break the Gazala line and capture Tobruk; Eighth Army held the defended boxes and port.
pre.forces: The Gazala defenders included 50th and South African divisions and Free French at Bir Hakeim. Axis mobile forces included 15th and 21st Panzer, 90th Light, Ariete and Trieste.
pre.deployment: The British line ran south from Gazala through fortified boxes and minefields. Axis mobile forces moved around the southern end near Bir Hakeim.

timeline.event: The Axis attack opened with a southern armoured move around Bir Hakeim.
Tobruk fell after the Gazala position had been defeated.

post.outcome: The Gazala line collapsed, Tobruk was taken and Eighth Army withdrew toward Egypt.
post.why: The mobile battle around boxes, minefields and supply routes broke the defence; the fall of Tobruk removed the port and accelerated the retreat.

battles.limits: The 2 June parliamentary account is contemporary and reports only the battle's opening, not its final result. The trial lacks the Cauldron supply crisis, minefield breaches, serviceability and full dated rosters.

battles.title: The retreat to the Alamein line

pre.objective: Axis forces pursued Eighth Army into Egypt; the Commonwealth sought a defensible line that would protect Alexandria and the Delta.
pre.forces: The pursuing Axis mobile army faced battered Eighth Army formations. Precise daily serviceable tanks, losses and unit positions remain unverified in the trial.
pre.deployment: After Tobruk fell, the pursuit moved east across the frontier and through the Matruh approaches toward the narrower Alamein position.

timeline.event: The Axis pursuit continued east after Tobruk's fall.
Axis forces approached El Alamein.

post.outcome: Eighth Army reached and defended the Alamein bottleneck before the next Axis attack.
post.why: The narrowing between the Mediterranean and Qattara Depression offered a shorter front after the open-desert retreat.

battles.limits: The chapter's carried counterfactual position may differ radically from the historical retreat. The model does not reconstruct each dated rearguard action or equipment loss.

battles.title: The First Battle of El Alamein

pre.objective: Eighth Army aimed to stop the Axis advance at Alamein and then counterattack; Axis forces sought to break through toward Alexandria and the Delta.
pre.forces: British Commonwealth formations, reinforced by the 9th Australian Division on 4 July, faced the exhausted Axis mobile force. Exact July brigade strengths and working tank returns are not yet in the trial.
pre.deployment: The front narrowed between the Mediterranean and the Qattara Depression, allowing a more continuous defence than the retreating open-desert line.

timeline.event: Axis troops attacked the new Alamein positions.
The 9th Australian Division joined Eighth Army in the battle area.
Australian attacks during 21–22 July broke into parts of the enemy line but could not be exploited fully.

post.outcome: The Axis advance was stopped; Commonwealth counterattacks gained ground locally but did not destroy the enemy position.
post.why: Axis exhaustion and the restricted front helped the defence, while coordination and armoured support limited exploitation of British gains.

battles.limits: The trial lacks full July strength returns, minefield detail and a verified defence map. The AWM account's 21–22 July action is one example rather than a complete daily battle log.

battles.title: The Battle of Alam Halfa

pre.objective: The Axis attempted to turn Eighth Army's southern flank; Montgomery's force aimed to hold the prepared Alamein position.
pre.forces: Axis mobile formations attacked a stronger British Commonwealth army, including the 9th Australian Division in the coastal sector. The trial's serviceable equipment and training are still estimated.
pre.deployment: The Axis move sought the southern approach near Alam Halfa Ridge while the Commonwealth held a defended line across the Alamein bottleneck.

timeline.event: The Axis attack opened around the southern flank.
Axis troops began withdrawing after air attack and dwindling fuel supplies.

post.outcome: The Axis attack failed to break through the Alamein position.
post.why: British material strength, air attack and Axis fuel shortage made the southern turn unsustainable.

battles.limits: The battle chapter continues to 6 September for game continuity; the AWM account dates Axis withdrawal to 2 September. The trial lacks detailed fuel, air and serviceability mechanisms.

battles.title: The Second Battle of El Alamein

pre.objective: Eighth Army planned to breach the fortified Axis line, defeat its armour and exploit west; Axis command aimed to hold the Alamein position.
pre.forces: XXX and XIII Corps provided major infantry forces while X Corps was the armoured exploitation formation. New Zealand troops participated in the main attacks. Full October brigade and serviceable equipment returns remain open for the trial.
pre.deployment: The armies faced one another across minefields and fortified positions spanning the Alamein bottleneck.

timeline.event: Operation Lightfoot began and New Zealand troops took Miteiriya Ridge.
Operation Supercharge opened the way for British armoured exploitation.
The Axis line was broken and withdrawal westward began.

post.outcome: Eighth Army defeated the Axis Alamein position and began a westward pursuit.
post.why: The breach operations and sustained fighting wore down the defended line and enabled armoured exploitation.

battles.limits: The game's October rosters, mine breaching, artillery preparation, training and serviceable tank flows are not yet historically validated.

battles.title: The November 1942 pursuit

pre.objective: Eighth Army pursued the withdrawing Axis army west from Egypt; Axis forces sought to preserve a fighting force and find another defensible line.
pre.forces: Eighth Army's infantry and mobile corps followed the Axis withdrawal. The game uses broad aggregate counters rather than a verified November march roster.
pre.deployment: After the Alamein breakthrough, the Axis line gave way and the pursuit followed the coastal route across the Egyptian frontier into Cyrenaica.

timeline.event: Axis forces were driven out of Egypt in the New Zealand campaign timeline.
Eighth Army retook Tobruk.
British troops recovered Benghazi.

post.outcome: By the end of November the historical Axis army had withdrawn west of Benghazi while Eighth Army held Egypt and recovered Tobruk and Benghazi.
post.why: The broken Alamein line and continued Commonwealth pressure forced a long withdrawal rather than a renewed battle for eastern Cyrenaica.

battles.limits: The trial's strategic verdict judges only the player's actual final holdings. Its 10 km map and broad counters do not validate the historical speed, stocks or losses of the pursuit.
